newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN to check malnourished N. Korea children.
newsitem.headline: UN to check malnourished N. Korea children.

text.p: The United Nations' food agency said on Tuesday it would start checking the height and weight of 3,500 to 4,000 children in North Korea so as to assess the extent of malnutrition across the drought-stricken state.

Christiane Berthiaume, spokeswoman of the World Food Programme (WFP), said the situation of children had deteriorated during the heat wave of the last several months which has wiped out 70 per cent of the maize harvest. Virtually no rain has fallen since July, depleting most reservoirs.

North Korea, already hit by two years of devastating floods and on the edge of mass starvation, has agreed to allow WFP to conduct a country-wide nutritional evaluation. It is expected to start in the next few days and last until late September.
"We are very pleased that we have reached a common understanding with North Korea to do this assessment," Judith Katona-Apte, head of WFP's team, was quoted as saying.
Four teams, composed of four people each including two experts from North Korea's Institute of Child Nutrition, are to examine infants and children at 18 sites, Berthiaume said.
"We are targeting children because they are the most vulnerable group," she told a news briefing in Geneva. "Their situation has deteriorated during the last two to three months."
"It is a major sampling. It is rare to be authorised to carry out an evaluation on such a large group," she added. "It will allow us to measure the extent of malnutrition throughout the country."
WFP also said its aid programme was making a difference.

In South Hamgyong province, school attendance has risen to 95 per cent from 15 per cent since the agency started providing supplementary maize and cooking oil, according to the spokeswoman. Children receive two meals and a snack daily.
